dataflow.outcome: A normal account receives server credentials.
dataflow.summary: readConfig complete object -> buildServer -> CoveService public parameter property -> usage limits -> authenticated JSON response

impact.why: Authentication and deployment secrets leave the server boundary.

likelihood.why: The Account screen requests the endpoint during normal use.

reachability.summary: Any verified human account can call the route. Email verification and ownership protect user data but do not authorize server secrets.

attackPath.summary: A self-registered user verifies email, signs in, and opens Account or GET /api/usage; the response exposes server-only configuration.

codeEvidence.explanation: A verified account is sufficient to invoke usage; there is no operator-only boundary.
codeEvidence.label: Verified-account usage route

codeEvidence.explanation: The caller supplies the complete parsed server configuration, which includes credential fields.
codeEvidence.label: Complete runtime configuration enters domain service

codeEvidence.explanation: TypeScript Pick constrains the declared type but the parameter property retains the original object at runtime.
codeEvidence.label: Type-only narrowing preserves extra runtime keys

codeEvidence.explanation: Fastify serializes the original configuration as the limits field; no response schema removes credential keys.
codeEvidence.label: Unfiltered object returned in account response

confidence.rationale: The complete configuration is passed unchanged, stored by a TypeScript parameter property, and serialized without a runtime allowlist.

evidence: packages/domain/service.ts constructor stores public limits with TypeScript Pick
originalCandidates.title: Usage endpoint returns full server configuration

findings.remediation: Construct an explicit runtime allowlist of the three public numeric limits and return only those values. Add a regression test with sentinel extra configuration fields; rotate any credentials if the vulnerable endpoint was exposed to untrusted users.
remediationTests: Assert service limits and the GET /api/usage limits object contain exactly MAX_PROJECTS, MAX_REVISIONS, MAX_STORAGE_BYTES even when constructor input has sentinel credential fields.

rootCause.summary: The server passes its entire configuration to CoveService. A TypeScript Pick is used only as a static annotation, so the parameter property retains every runtime key. usage returns that same object to an ordinary verified account, crossing the server-secret boundary.

severity.rationale: High impact credential disclosure is directly reachable by self-registered verified accounts. Further misuse depends on credential scope and network reachability.

findings.summary: Any verified account can request the usage summary and receive the full runtime configuration, including the authentication secret, database URL, and configured SMTP credentials.
findings.title: Usage summary exposes server credentials to account owners

limitations: No production service is deployed; severity describes the supplied production code path.
Downstream database or SMTP compromise was not exercised.
validation.method: independent focused source investigation and parent static validation
validation.summary: The parent independently read configuration construction, constructor storage, verified-account route and JSON sink. These establish credential disclosure without reading or reproducing credential values.

dataflow.source: Server-held SMTP credential and recovery message
dataflow.summary: Production SMTP configuration -> Nodemailer optional STARTTLS -> SMTP credentials and account links

impact.why: Recovery links can authorize account access.

likelihood.why: Requires active network interference with a supported deployment option.

reachability.summary: Conditional on SMTP_SECURE=false and an active network attacker; no unprivileged application user alone can trigger interception.

attackPath.summary: An attacker on the configured SMTP network path removes STARTTLS from the server response; secure:false without requireTLS permits authentication and reset mail over the unencrypted connection.

codeEvidence.explanation: When secure=false, no requireTLS option forces successful STARTTLS before authentication or message delivery.
codeEvidence.label: SMTP transport permits optional TLS

codeEvidence.explanation: The same transport sends account verification and password recovery URLs.
codeEvidence.label: Authentication email contains sensitive links

confidence.rationale: Application transport omits requireTLS; the installed Nodemailer implementation only upgrades when advertised or required.

originalCandidates.evidence: apps/api/auth.ts:10-16 secure false default without requireTLS; nodemailer connect then login when server omits STARTTLS
originalCandidates.title: Production SMTP allows opportunistic STARTTLS downgrade

findings.remediation: Require successful TLS in production: implicit TLS with secure=true or requireTLS=true when secure=false. Keep local Mailpit plaintext limited to development. Add a transport test proving a non-STARTTLS server never receives AUTH or message data in production.
remediationTests: Assert production transport requires STARTTLS when implicit TLS is disabled.
Use a local controlled SMTP fixture without STARTTLS and assert rejection before authentication.

rootCause.summary: Production accepts SMTP_SECURE=false, intended for STARTTLS. makeAuth passes secure:false and credentials to Nodemailer without requireTLS. Installed Nodemailer upgrades only when STARTTLS is advertised or requireTLS is set, so omission of that capability allows plaintext authentication and messages.

severity.rationale: High-impact credential or account recovery exposure requires an active attacker on the API-to-SMTP network path and the supported STARTTLS configuration.

findings.summary: The supported SMTP_SECURE=false production configuration permits opportunistic STARTTLS. A network attacker who suppresses STARTTLS advertisement can receive SMTP authentication and verification or recovery messages over plaintext.
findings.title: Production SMTP can send credentials and recovery links without TLS

limitations: Requires a production STARTTLS deployment and active network position; implicit TLS configuration is unaffected.
validation.method: Independent baseline source investigation and parent source validation
validation.summary: Parent read transport options, production validation and Nodemailer smtp-connection STARTTLS condition at installed dist/esm/smtp-connection/index.js:1227-1230. No mail interception or real credential testing occurred.
